Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

increase verb and noun

also grow, go up, make bigger, growth, multiply

classical

Cic. Sen. 46: quae mihi sermōnis aviditātem auxit
Liv. 21.33.6: quōs nemora etiam repercussaeque vallēs augēbant

augeō, augēre, auxī, auctum

verb, second conjugation, transitive

increase, make greater

Transitive; in the passive, “to increase, grow”.

Other words

  • crēscō, crēscere, crēvī, crētum — increase, grow

    verb, third conjugation, intransitive · classical · Liv. 3.26.4: crēvit ex metū aliēnō, ut fit, audācia; Plin. Ep. 9.33.6: crēscit audācia experīmentō

    Of what grows or increases by itself.

  • incrēmentum, incrēmentī n. — increase, growth

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 52: vītium ortūs, satūs, incrēmenta; Quint. 11.2.41: sēnsum incrēmentī

  • multiplicō, multiplicāre, multiplicāvī, multiplicātum — multiply, increase many times over

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.32 (Lewis & Short); Ov. Rem. 98: plūrima collēctīs multiplicantur aquīs

    Of what grows many times over, as a river does by gathering streams; in arithmetic, to multiply (see multiply).

Examples

  • habeōque senectūtī magnam grātiam, quae mihi sermōnis aviditātem auxit, pōtiōnis et cibī sustulit

    and I am very grateful to old age, which has increased my appetite for conversation and taken away my appetite for food and drinkCic. Sen. 46

  • crēvit ex metū aliēnō, ut fit, audācia

    as usually happens, their boldness grew with the other side’s fearLiv. 3.26.4

  • crēscit audācia experīmentō

    courage grows by tryingPlin. Ep. 9.33.6

  • flūmina pauca vidēs dē magnīs fontibus orta: plūrima collēctīs multiplicantur aquīs

    few rivers, you see, rise from great springs; most grow by gathering watersOv. Rem. 97–98

See also make smaller, develop, grow, multiply.
